notes: Target: build an in-IDE PR review assistant for enterprise customers (VS Code + JetBrains).
Wants low-latency streaming for single-line comment suggestions and multi-line diff summaries; first-token latency target <= 200ms, steady-state per-token ~50-150ms depending on model and batching.
Primary features: automated diff summarization, high-signal comment generation (security, style, test coverage), reranking of generated comments using repo-specific signals.
'Need model pinning and deterministic rollbacks — we must be able to lock to a vetted model build per customer and fallback automatically.' — CTO (Paul Kim).
POC constraints: anonymized PR corpus of ~10k diffs, PR sizes up to 1200 LOC; want to measure suggestion precision@3 and false-positive rate for security recommendations.
Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to pay premium for consistently low latency in the editor but care about per-token cost at scale (multi-repo orgs).
Preference: open-model compatibility and quantized variants for Dedicated/Private; also interested in Redwood verified profiles for baseline comparisons.
Integration: GitHub Apps + Actions for CI hooks, ability to route heavy reranking to cheaper batch model while serving lightweight streaming suggestions from a low-latency model.
Security: SSO + SAML required, audit logging for all generated suggestions, KMS integration for keys, and EU data residency for key enterprise accounts.
Legal asked for data retention & deletion flow; product team proposed ephemeral KV cache + configurable retention (30/90/365 days).
Demo feedback (2025-01-30): reviewers liked streaming previews in VS Code; some comments on hallucination in bigger diffs — suggested sandboxed evals and example-driven prompt templates.
Internal ask: SE to draft recommended routing policy (low-latency model for first-pass + batch rerank for final suggestions) and cost estimates for 50k PRs/month.
Requested artifacts: security FAQ, on-prem deployment guide, dedicated latency SLOs, sample pricing model tied to token tiers (drive link shared).
